The report enumerates the ordering invariant's three consumers — the cursor payload, the cursor-keyed client cache, and the export watermark — and treats them separately: the sort change goes to (pinned, created_at), while the export job deliberately keeps the created_at watermark so pin changes cannot affect incremental export.

Old-sort cursors are handled explicitly: a versioned composite cursor (version 2 with lastPinned) replaces the implicit shape, decodeCursor accepts exactly the legacy and v2 shapes and rejects everything else with the domain error, and legacy cursors continue their pagination under the legacy ordering to completion so in-flight readers neither miss nor duplicate rows. Legacy and composite cursors produce distinct cache keys.
